name: i-have-adhd
description: A skill to stop your coding agent from burying the answer. ADHD-friendly output.
one_liner: A plug-in for AI coding assistants that forces them to answer with the next concrete step first, instead of burying it in a paragraph of preamble.
buyer: A solo developer who already pays for Claude Code or a similar coding assistant and is tired of scrolling past chatty explanations to find the actual command to run.
business_use_cases: A freelance developer installs it across every client project so every AI session gives numbered, actionable steps instead of essays.
A coding bootcamp bundles it into their standard toolchain setup so students get terser, easier-to-follow AI guidance.
An engineering manager standardizes it org-wide as a lightweight house style for how AI assistants talk to the team.

money_ideas.idea: Sell a 'pro' pack of tuned output styles (concise, verbose, exec-summary) for different roles as a one-time purchase.
Offer a hosted config/preferences dashboard for teams to standardize and sync this style across everyone's agent, billed per seat.

steal_this: Package three or four 'response style' presets (terse, ADHD-friendly, exec-summary, ELI5) as a $9 one-time Gumroad pack for coding-agent power users this weekend.
